title: Alert counts tripled after the plant's WAN outage
scenario: After a 3-hour WAN outage and a flaky replacement router, the cloud dashboard shows two to three times the normal events for 09:00-13:00 on every pump and planners raised work orders off duplicates. The gateway buffered locally as designed; the log is full of NTP drift warnings.
task: Find why the cloud holds more events than the gateway produced, with evidence
Rule the clock drift in or out
Make replay exactly-once under lost acks, partial acks, restarts and re-emitted readings
Plan the cleanup of duplicates and work orders
acceptance: Cloud counts equal gateway counts on the outage day, also with 90% lost acks
Partial acks leave unacknowledged rows pending; ids stable across resends
Order per device preserved; buffer cap still enforced
ANSWER.md: root cause with evidence, red herring, cleanup plan
